intro: A home in Nashville, a suburban property near Knoxville and a similarly priced residence in Memphis can have noticeably different monthly ownership expenses. Property taxes, insurance premiums, mortgage interest and association fees all influence how much house you can comfortably afford.

Our free Tennessee mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly housing payment before purchasing a property. Enter your home price, down payment, interest rate and loan term, then include property taxes, homeowners insurance and other applicable expenses to establish a realistic homebuying budget.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Tennessee?

blocks.markdown:
A $285,000 Tennessee home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,366.98.

Including illustrative property taxes and insurance produces the following estimate.

This example assumes no private mortgage insurance or association fees. The interest rate, property taxes and insurance premiums are illustrative planning assumptions rather than current statewide averages.

Tennessee offers housing opportunities across metropolitan neighborhoods, suburban developments, mountain communities and rural areas.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Tennessee housing statistics](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/TN/POP060220), the median value of owner-occupied homes was $286,700 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among homeowners with mortgages were $1,566, while approximately 66.9% of occupied housing units were owner-occupied.

These historical statistics include existing homeowners who purchased properties under different market conditions. They do not represent current property asking prices or mortgage offers.

Housing expenses in Nashville, Franklin and other popular metropolitan communities may differ considerably from those in smaller towns.

Buyers considering mountain properties should also investigate insurance availability, road maintenance and transportation expenses.

Research recent comparable property sales within your preferred community before establishing your purchase budget.

sections.heading: How to Use the Tennessee Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Start by entering the expected purchase price of your home and the amount you intend to contribute as a down payment.

Select your preferred repayment period and enter the annual mortgage interest rate quoted by your lender.

If you have not received a quote, consult [Freddie Mac's mortgage market survey](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms) for a national reference.

Next, enter annual property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums and monthly association fees.

Include private mortgage insurance if required by your conventional financing arrangement.

Review the estimated monthly housing payment and adjust individual inputs to compare borrowing scenarios.

The amortization schedule shows how much of each payment goes toward interest and reducing your outstanding mortgage balance.

Our national Mortgage Calculator also allows you to compare financing arrangements outside Tennessee.

sections.heading: How Tennessee Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Tennessee calculates real estate taxes using appraised property values, statutory assessment ratios and applicable local tax rates.

Local assessors determine property valuations, while county and municipal governments establish tax rates to support public services.

### Tennessee residential property assessment ratio

According to the [Tennessee Department of Revenue's property tax guidance](https://www.tn.gov/revenue/taxes/local-taxes/property-tax.html), residential real estate generally has an assessment ratio of 25%.

For example, a residential property appraised at $285,000 would have an assessed value of $71,250.

The 25% assessment ratio establishes the value used for taxation. It does not mean homeowners pay 25% of their property's market value in annual taxes.

Local property tax rates are applied to the assessed value.

### Tennessee property tax calculation example

Suppose a home has an appraised value of $285,000 and a hypothetical combined property tax rate of $2.50 per $100 of assessed value.

Actual taxes depend on your property's assessment, county, municipality and applicable adjustments.

If a property lies within city limits, make sure your estimate includes both municipal and county taxes where applicable.

Contact your county assessor or local tax collecting official for current property-specific information.

Tennessee permits participating local governments to offer a property tax freeze to qualifying older homeowners.

The [Tennessee Comptroller's Property Tax Freeze program](https://comptroller.tn.gov/office-functions/pa/property-taxes/property-tax-programs/property-tax-freeze.html) generally requires applicants to be at least 65 years old, own and occupy their primary residence and satisfy applicable annual income limits.

Qualifying homeowners can retain a base property tax amount while continuing to meet program requirements.

Income limits vary by jurisdiction. For 2026, Davidson and Knox counties have adopted the higher local-option income limit of $63,470.

Property improvements or purchasing a different residence can result in changes to the frozen tax amount.

The program is not available automatically throughout Tennessee. Verify local participation and eligibility before reducing your estimated property tax expenses.

Tennessee homeowners may experience severe thunderstorms, tornadoes, hail, flooding and other weather-related damage.

Insurance costs depend on property location, construction materials, rebuilding costs, roof condition and selected coverage.

The [Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance's homeowners insurance guidance](https://www.tn.gov/commerce/insurance/consumer-edu/homeowners/focus.html) explains how property characteristics and environmental exposure can influence insurance premiums.

Obtain several property-specific quotes before completing your purchase.

### Tornado, wind and hail coverage

Review whether your homeowners insurance policy includes separate deductibles for wind or hail damage.

Ask your insurer whether roof claims are settled using replacement cost or actual cash value.

For example, a hypothetical 2% deductible on $300,000 in dwelling coverage would represent $6,000 in potential out-of-pocket expenses for an applicable covered claim.

A cheaper annual premium may result in greater financial responsibility after property damage.

### Flood and earthquake insurance

Standard homeowners insurance generally excludes flooding and earthquake damage.

Properties near rivers and low-lying areas may require separate flood protection. Homeowners in western Tennessee should also investigate earthquake exposure when comparing insurance options.

Use the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) to investigate flood risks.

Include applicable additional insurance premiums in the calculator without counting overlapping coverage twice.
The following estimates assume a 20% down payment, 6% fixed annual interest and a 30-year mortgage.

These estimates exclude property taxes, homeowners insurance, PMI and association fees.

Compare complete monthly housing expenses rather than relying exclusively on principal and interest.

The Tennessee Housing Development Agency, commonly known as THDA, offers mortgage financing and purchase assistance through approved lenders.

### Great Choice Home Loan

The [THDA Great Choice Home Loan program](https://thda.org/homebuyers/first-time-homebuyers/) provides eligible borrowers with 30-year fixed-rate mortgage financing.

Applicants generally need a minimum credit score of 640 and must satisfy county-specific household income and purchase price limits.

Qualifying repeat buyers may also participate under certain circumstances, including purchases in designated targeted areas or eligible military status.

### Great Choice Plus deferred assistance

The [Great Choice Plus assistance program](https://thda.org/homebuyers/down-payment-assistance/) offers qualifying borrowers deferred assistance of up to $6,000 or $10,000, depending on the applicable option.

The assistance is provided through an interest-free secondary mortgage without scheduled monthly payments.

It can be forgiven after ten years. Selling or refinancing before the forgiveness period ends can require full repayment.

### Great Choice Plus amortizing assistance

Eligible borrowers may also receive assistance equal to 5% of the property's sales price, capped at $15,000.

This option requires monthly repayments over 30 years at the same interest rate as the associated first mortgage.

For example, 5% assistance on a $285,000 property would amount to $14,250.

At an illustrative 6% interest rate over 30 years, this second mortgage would add approximately $85.44 to the borrower's monthly expenses.

### Assistance for newly constructed homes

THDA also offers qualifying buyers of newly built or proposed construction properties assistance of up to $25,000.

The secondary loan carries no interest and is repaid over 15 years.

Receiving the full $25,000 would produce an additional monthly payment of approximately $138.89.

Include secondary mortgage payments when estimating complete housing expenses. Confirm funding, eligibility and financing terms with a participating lender.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning a Tennessee Home

blocks.markdown:
Homeowners should prepare for expenses beyond their regular mortgage payments.

Summer cooling, property maintenance, pest control and storm-related repairs can affect household budgets.

Properties in mountainous or rural areas may require private well maintenance, septic servicing and access road repairs.

Condominium buyers should review association fees, reserve funds and potential special assessments.

Arrange a professional inspection and request historical utility information before purchasing a property.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Tennessee?

blocks.markdown:
Begin with reliable monthly take-home income and subtract existing financial obligations.

Tennessee does not impose an individual state income tax on wages, although federal income taxes and applicable payroll deductions still reduce available earnings.

Our [Tennessee Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/tennessee-paycheck-calculator/) can help estimate take-home pay, while our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) can help evaluate existing borrowing commitments.

Compare mortgage offers using the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

Maintain sufficient savings for closing expenses, insurance deductibles and unexpected repairs rather than committing your entire cash balance to the down payment.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $285,000 Tennessee home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, monthly principal and interest would be approximately $1,366.98. Property taxes, homeowners insurance and applicable fees increase the total housing payment.

### How are Tennessee residential property taxes calculated?

Residential properties generally use a 25% assessment ratio. Applicable county and municipal property tax rates are then applied to assessed value, with adjustments for qualifying relief programs and other applicable charges.

### Does Tennessee offer $25,000 in down payment assistance?

Yes. THDA offers qualifying buyers of newly built or proposed construction homes up to $25,000 through an interest-free second mortgage repayable over 15 years. Other assistance options are available for eligible buyers of existing properties.
